payload.question: How much outside money did the council bring into the city?
payload.label: External funding brought in against target, 2024/25
payload.council_caveat: One award is nearly all of it. The council's own note lists inside the £42,678,427: "£35,000,000 from Homes England for the Anglia Square redevelopment to build a new community of affordable homes, retail, office and leisure spaces", £104,625 from Homes England for East Norwich due diligence, and £520,000 from Sport England for solar panels at Riverside Leisure Centre. The council publishes these numbers as screenshots of a dashboard inside a PDF, so they cannot be read by machine. We read them off the images by eye, which is why this measure is flagged for human checking.
payload.evidence: The council sets itself a target of bringing in £250,000 a year of outside funding for development and regeneration. In 2024/25 it reported £42,678,427, against £463,086 the year before. A single large award swings this figure enormously, so one year on its own says little. This indicator has no intervention level published, so the general target rule applies.
